title: StratusWorks POC: quality guardrails and benchmarking plan
summary: POC scoping focused on defining success criteria for a quality-first pilot: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination detection rules, format checking, scoring rubric, workload sizing and a 4-week timeline for initial benchmarks.
next_steps: Alex to send POC deck + proposed rubrics link
Priya to draft initial golden prompt set and scoring spreadsheet
StratusWorks to provide sample dataset (5k records) and final success metrics by 2026-12-28
action_items: Priya Nair - prepare golden prompts (10 canonical prompts + 20 variants) - due 2026-12-27
Alex Rivera - share POC deck, security one-pager, and eval spreadsheet - due 2026-12-21
Sam Lopez - upload sample dataset and redaction rules to shared drive - due 2026-12-28
Jenna Park - confirm network/VPC constraints and KMS requirements - due 2026-12-23
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (StratusWorks Head of Data), Jenna (Platform Eng), Marcus (CTO)

[00:00] Alex: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we wanna make today real practical, um, set clear success criteria for the pilot, and make sure the benchmarking plan is actionable.
[00:12] Sam: Yep, thanks Alex. We're really focused on reducing downsteam handoffs from our support team, so quality is the main KPI — precision on entity extraction and hallucination rate under 1% ideally, but we want realistic numbers.
[00:26] Jenna: Also need to surface the output format strictly. If the model deviates from JSON schema our parsers break, so format checks are critical.
[00:36] Alex: Totally. Priya and I sketched a three-part quality eval: 1) golden prompt suite, 2) regression test set, 3) automated hallucination and format checks. We'll talk through each.
[00:49] Priya: Quick note — when we say "golden prompts" we mean canonical prompts that produce the expected structure and semantic answer from the model. We'll create variants to test sensitivity.
[00:58] Marcus: How many golden prompts are we talking? We don't want to over-index on a tiny set.
[01:05] Priya: Good call. Proposal is 10 canonical prompts covering top intents + 20 adversarial/edge variants. Each prompt will have pass/fail rules and a scoring weight.
[01:16] Sam: Pass/fail rules are cool, but we also need graded scoring for partial credit — sometimes an extraction is 90% correct.
[01:23] Priya: We'll use a hybrid rubric: binary checks for format/schema compliance, and continuous metrics for content quality (F1 for extractions, BLEU-ish for short text responses, precision/recall where applicable).
[01:34] Jenna: On format checks, can Redwood emit a structured validation log? Like which field failed type/schema and why?
[01:40] Alex: Yes — our eval harness will include schema validation and produce per-token/parsing error traces. We'll share a sample report.
[01:48] Sam: Hallucination detection — what's your approach? We need to detect unsupported facts, not just hallucinated numbers.
[01:55] Priya: Multi-layered: first heuristic checks (sourceable fields vs free text), then entailment models to score claim supportability, plus token-level uncertainty thresholds. We'll flag candidate hallucinations and attach a confidence score.
[02:08] Marcus: That sounds compute-heavy. Will that blow up the cost of the POC?
[02:13] Alex: We can toggle the depth. For baseline runs we'll run lighter heuristics; for deeper analysis we'll run a routed batch overnight on Dedicated or a higher-performance instance if you prefer. We'll estimate cost in the deck.
[02:24] Sam: OK. Workload sizing — our support use case is about 120 requests/minute peak, average 40 rpm. Many requests are short (single-turn), some contain long context (~1k tokens).
[02:36] Priya: For the POC benchmarks we recommend a staged load plan: functional correctness at low concurrency, then a 10-minute sustained run at 40 rpm, and two 5-minute spikes to 120 rpm. We'll also run a few multi-turn sessions with 1k context.
[02:52] Alex: We'll include KV/prefix cache settings to optimize latency for repeated dialogs. Also suggest running with and without quantization/compaction to measure quality tradeoffs.
[03:03] Jenna: Network constraints — we are VPC-only and must use our KMS for keys; we also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[03:11] Alex: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit exports, we'll include config steps in the security appendix. I'll send the SOC2/ISO artifacts.
[03:19] Sam: Success criteria — define pass thresholds for the POC so we can decide to expand. My draft: schema compliance >= 99%, entity extraction F1 >= 0.88, hallucination rate <= 1.5% (token-weighted), end-to-end parse success >= 95%.
[03:36] Priya: Those are reasonable. We suggest adding a human review pass for edge cases — a sampling plan of 200 outputs for human judgment to calibrate automated metrics.
[03:45] Marcus: Timeline? We want initial results before fiscal Q1 planning.
[03:49] Alex: Suggested timeline: week 0 (this week) — align on success criteria and golden prompts; week 1 — Redwoods runs baseline bench on sample dataset; week 2 — run scaled load tests and hallucination analysis; week 3 — incorporate feedback, run regression suite; week 4 — deliver final evaluation and decision deck. So approx 4 weeks.
[04:09] Sam: Can you put that as a calendar view with milestone owners?
[04:13] Alex: Yep, will share Gantt-style milestones.
[04:16] Jenna: About regression tests — we need tests that fail when a new model version degrades on critical intents. How do you handle model rollbacks?
[04:24] Priya: We'll design a regression playlist of ~500 golden examples with threshold checks. If a candidate model drops below threshold we fail the rollout. Redwood supports canary rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model.
[04:36] Sam: Will the regression be deterministic across runs? We need reproducibility.
[04:41] Priya: We'll pin seeds where possible, freeze prompt templates, and version datasets in the eval harness. Some non-determinism remains for sampling decoders — we'll capture variance stats and require stability gates.
[04:54] Alex: A couple practical items — please share a representative 5k sample (anonymized) and a short list of top 20 intents. Priya will send a template for prompt annotations.
[05:05] Sam: We'll get that uploaded by Monday. Jenna, can you confirm network constraints?
[05:09] Jenna: Yes, I can. We'll need a small IP allowlist and the KMS integration details.
[05:14] Marcus: Regarding competitors — we've already tried a quick proof on other vendors and saw better latency with Redwood's runtime, but we need to validate hallucination figures.
[05:24] Alex: Noted — we'll include side-by-side baseline comparisons in the appendix, but main focus is your thresholds.
[05:29] Sam: Scoring approach — I want a single composite score for stakeholder signoff, but with drill-down. Thoughts?
[05:35] Priya: Composite index works: weighted sum of schema compliance (25%), extraction F1 (35%), hallucination penalty (30%, inverted), and latency/ops (10%). Each subscore is explainable in the dashboard. You can tweak weights.
[05:48] Sam: That helps. Make sure hallucination penalty is aggressive — even small hallucinations are costly for us.
[05:53] Priya: We'll provide a sensitivity matrix showing how composite score changes with different hallucination thresholds.
[05:59] Alex: Next steps recap: we'll send the POC deck, eval spreadsheet, security pack. Priya will produce the initial golden prompt set. StratusWorks will upload sample data and confirm infra constraints. We'll target a baseline run first week of January.
[06:13] Marcus: Are there any blockers on your side?
[06:16] Alex: No blockers. If anything, getting the sample data and KMS info quickly will keep the timeline.
[06:22] Jenna: One last Q — can we get a quick demo of the hallucination detection output during the baseline run? A visual would help stakeholders.
[06:29] Priya: Yes, we can include a dashboard screenshot and annotated examples in the baseline report.
[06:34] Sam: Great. Thanks everyone.
[06:36] Alex: Thanks, we'll follow up with links. End.

Artifacts referenced: POC deck (https://redwood.app/links/stratus-poc-deck), eval spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/links/stratus-eval-sheet), security one-pager (https://redwood.app/links/stratus-security).
notes: Transcript includes natural disfluencies, occasional label 'Alex' repeated; minor transcription errors expected (e.g., 'downsteam' instead of 'downstream').
